questions.q: A quarter starts with 150 open cases, 1,240 are opened, and 1,180 are closed. What is the ending backlog?
Why is a report of cases opened per month not enough to prove the queue is growing?
options: Salesforce cannot count cases by month
Opened cases are always equal to closed cases
Backlog depends on how many cases are closed as well as opened
Case volume never changes over time
questions.explain: The queue grows only when more cases come in than go out, so you need the closed count too.

questions.q: What is a risk of relying only on an average resolution time?
options: Averages cannot be calculated on cases
A few very old cases can pull the average up, so compare it with the maximum or a median
Averages always understate the true time
questions.explain: Outliers distort averages. Looking at Max, a median if available, or the distribution gives a more honest picture.

questions.q: Which statement about calendar hours versus business hours is correct?
options: Calendar hours ignore nights and weekends
Business hours are always the default in standard reports
There is no difference between them
Calendar hours include nights and weekends, so you should say which clock your resolution time uses
questions.explain: A case opened on Friday evening looks slow on a calendar clock. Business-hours logic needs extra setup, so always state your clock.

questions.q: Why run a SOQL count grouped by Priority alongside the volume report?
options: SOQL replaces the need for any report
It reaches the same total by an independent route, which reconciles your report
questions.explain: Two independent routes to the same total is reconciliation, and it catches filter mistakes in the report.
